---
title: "Getting started"
subtitle: "Three ways to use this project, depending on where you want the container to run."
---

## Pick an entry point

::: {.codespaces-grid}

::: {.codespaces-card}

### [GitHub Codespaces](codespaces.qmd)

Open a container in the browser or in your desktop editor, with nothing installed locally.
Best for trying Quarto, running a workshop, or reproducing a bug report.

:::

::: {.codespaces-card}

### [Dev Containers](dev-containers.qmd)

Run the same container on your own machine with Docker and the Dev Containers extension or CLI.
Best for day-to-day work on an existing project.

:::

::: {.codespaces-card}

### [As a template](template.qmd)

Copy the repository and keep only the configuration you need.
Best when you want your own project to ship a Quarto container.

:::

:::

## The quickest path

Launch a Codespace on this repository with either image.

::: {.codespaces-actions}

::: {.codespaces-action}

[Purpose-built image]{.codespaces-action-label}

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces with the purpose-built image](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/mcanouil/quarto-codespaces?quickstart=1&devcontainer_path=.devcontainer%2Fdevcontainer.json)

Uses [`ghcr.io/mcanouil/quarto-codespaces:latest`](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-codespaces/pkgs/container/quarto-codespaces), described in [container images](../reference/images.qmd).
Everything is preinstalled, so it starts fastest.

:::

::: {.codespaces-action}

[Universal base image]{.codespaces-action-label}

[![Open in GitHub Codespaces with the universal base image](https://github.com/codespaces/badge.svg)](https://codespaces.new/mcanouil/quarto-codespaces?quickstart=1&devcontainer_path=.devcontainer%2Funiversal%2Fdevcontainer.json)

Uses the `universal` configuration, built on Microsoft's Codespaces base image.
It consumes less of your GitHub storage quota.

:::

:::

## Then what?

Once the container is up, `quarto check` reports the state of every engine.
The [Quarto check output](../reference/quarto-check.qmd) page shows what the latest build produces, so you can compare against a known-good run.

Language environments are not created for you.
Run [`init-env.sh`](../reference/init-env.qmd) when you want a project-local `renv`, `uv`, or Julia environment.
